pairs.subject: browser-credential-boundary
pairs.evidence: src/app/leaderboard/page.tsx:121 The crawlable public register shows every anonymous visitor the backend family (e.g. 'Aurora DSQL'). /api/health hides that same dbMode behind CRON_SECRET as 'deployment TOPOLOGY ... shouldn't be handed to an anonymous caller' (src/app/api/health/route.ts:30). The topology opacity paid for at one door is published for free at another, which is the 'cheapest publication' failure the technique names.

techniques.evidence: src/app/leaderboard/page.tsx:121 The technique says opacity is only as strong as the fact's cheapest publication: either accept dbMode as public and drop the health-route gate, or stop rendering it here. Currently both are done. The failure-vs-empty half is fine: page.tsx:74 turns a thrown read into null, and the page shows RegisterUnavailable rather than an empty ranking.

src/lib/register/data.ts:162 The register is a server-side Prisma projection. No browser holds a store credential for these tables, so there is no public-role shape. The select is still narrow, and isPrivate is re-asserted per row.
src/app/portfolio/page.tsx:38 Each org is gated by canReadOrg in deployed code. No row policy is evaluated for a browser-held role.

pairs.registryProposal: opaque-upstream-errors' 'cheapest publication' section is written for an upstream hostname in the bundle. It could say explicitly that a coarse backend label shown on a public page is the same failure when a sibling route treats that label as topology to withhold, and that the fix is to make the two doors agree, either way.

pairs.subject: browser-credential-boundary
pairs.evidence: src/lib/integrations/ingest-token.ts:122 The per-org ingest token is a server-minted HMAC bound to the slug and a revocation epoch, never stored, and checked in constant time with no fallback secret. The ingest routes answer with a closed, status-mapped vocabulary (401/415/400/503 'not configured'/503 retry) and log raw store errors only on the server.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/integrations/ingest-token.ts:122 The carried token is sealed under a key only the server holds, bound to its subject (slug + epoch inside the signed material). With no secret, parseIngestToken returns null (line 98).

src/app/api/integrations/ingest/v1/metrics/route.ts:82 The store failure is logged and mapped to a retryable 503 with Retry-After. 'Not configured here' is its own member (ingest-guard.ts:141), and auth runs before the wire-format check.

src/lib/integrations/ingest-token.ts:40 The signing secret is an unprefixed server-only variable whose absence closes the door (no silent dev fallback). The module has no explicit `server-only` marker; it relies on node:crypto plus a comment that the client never imports it.

src/lib/integrations/ingest-token.ts:2 This is the technique's strongest home ('nowhere, derived on demand'): the token is recomputed from the slug and epoch, so there is no stored token column to expose.
src/lib/integrations/otlp.ts:25 The git.repository URL inside the OTLP payload is only parsed into a repo identity or a named unsupported host. It is never fetched, so no destination arrives as data.
